chapter.heading: For the music director. To the tune “Lilies.” A psalm (maskil) of the sons of Korah. A love song.
chapter.v:
I am
moved to write about this wonderful subject. Let me share what I have written for the king. What I say comes from the pen of a skilled author.

You are
more handsome than anyone else. You always speak graciously, for God has blessed you forever.

Strap on
your sword, mighty warrior, stride out in glory and majesty!

In your
majesty ride out to victory, in the defense of truth, humility, and right, because you are strong and act powerfully.

Your sharp
arrows pierce the hearts of your enemies; the nations fall under you.

Your throne
comes from God, and lasts forever and ever. The scepter with which you rule is a scepter of fairness.

You love
what is right and hate what is wrong. That is why God, your God, has placed you above everyone else by anointing you with the oil of joy.

Your robes
are perfumed with aloes, myrrh, and cassia; music played on stringed instruments in palaces decorated with ivory makes you happy.

The daughters
of kings are among the noblewomen; the queen stands beside you on your right, wearing jewelry made of gold from Ophir.

Listen to
what I have to say, daughter; please pay attention. Don't pine for your people and your family.

May the
king desire you in your beauty; respect him, for he is your lord.

The people
of Tyre will come with gifts; rich people will look for your favor.

Inside her
preparation room the princess bride looks wonderful in her golden gown.

Wearing her
beautiful clothes she is brought to the king, followed by her bridesmaids.

What a
happy, joyful procession enters the king's palace!

Your sons
will take the place of your fathers; as princes you will make them rulers throughout the land.

Through my
words you will be famous through all generations, and nations will praise you forever and ever.
